_comment: Digital Asset Links — THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for which Android apps may claim
jkOS links, and the file every TWA's link verification fetches from
https://<origin>/.well-known/assetlinks.json.
This file is not served directly. gen-nginx-weave.mjs EMBEDS the `targets`
array below into each generated prod server block and into jkAuth's
hand-tuned block in standalone.conf, so every origin answers with identical
JSON and the two cannot drift (`pnpm check:nginx` asserts it).
WHY IT IS NOT JUST A FILE IN public/: serveSpa mounts express.static, which
IGNORES DOTFILE PATHS by default, so `.well-known/` never matches — and the
`app.get('*')` SPA fallback then answers with index.html at 200. Android's
verifier receives HTML, fails, and reports nothing useful; the only symptom
is a browser URL bar that will not go away. Measured on the real server
before this existed: 200 text/html. It must be answered at the edge.
TO ADD AN APP: run `bubblewrap init`, take the SHA-256 of the signing key it
prints (or `keytool -list -v -keystore <ks>`), add an entry, regenerate
(`node infra/nginx/gen-nginx-weave.mjs`), and RESTART nginx — not reload,
the confs are bind-mounts and a reload will not re-read a replaced inode.
An empty `targets` array is valid JSON and serves correctly; verification
simply fails until a real fingerprint is added. That is the honest state
before the keystore exists, and it is preferable to a placeholder that looks
configured.
